run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network entry point nginx-thrift (Deployment nginx-thrift, pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qtqx5) is in a CrashLoopBackOff caused by an injected 16Mi memory limit. The pod's only container runs with resources.limits.memory=16Mi and resources.requests.memory=16Mi, was terminated OOMKilled with exit code 137 at 22:54:04 and 22:54:05Z, had restartCount 1 at 22:54:06Z and 3 by 22:55:00Z, and the Deployment reports Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable, unavailableReplicas=1). That 16Mi value does not come from the workload's own objects: both the Deployment nginx-thrift pod template and its ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 declare limits.memory=256Mi and requests.memory=128Mi, and no other pod in the namespace declares any memory limit at all. The value matches an admission-time mutator: ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in namespace platform-ops contains a Python admission webhook whose constant MEMORY = "16Mi" is stamped by a JSONPatch into container[0] resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory, and all five MutatingWebhookConfigurations in the cluster point their clientConfig at Service platform-policy-controller.platform-ops:443 /mutate, including gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration whose pods CREATE rule for namespace social-network has an empty objectSelector. That controller Deployment became available at 22:53:46Z; the nginx-thrift pod was re-created at 22:53:54-55Z after it, and is the only pod carrying the 16Mi limit. Client-side failures are visible in the load generator's log (wrk2-job pod: 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 42782' at 22:54:03Z and a burst of 'reconnect_socket' lines at 22:54:04Z) while kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="nginx-thrift"} stayed 0. Traces and span metrics do not cover the failure: the only nginx-web-server trace in the sample is a successful 200 at 22:53:48Z, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no series in 22:30-22:54Z, so error rates are unmeasured rather than zero. All other 26 application pods were Running with 0 restarts; media-frontend reported available=0 during its startup samples but its pod was Running/ready with 0 restarts, so it is checked and not placed in the affected group.

claims.text: Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qtqx5 (namespace social-network) ran its nginx-thrift container to termination with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at 2026-11-23T22:54:04Z and again at 2026-11-23T22:54:05Z, with restartCount 1 and Ready=False (containers with unready status: [nginx-thrift]) at the observed time.

The crash repeated: nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qtqx5 shows restartCount 3, lastState.terminated with exitCode 137, and container state waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 40s restarting failed container=nginx-thrift'), while its spec still carries limits.memory=16Mi.

The affected pod's 16Mi memory limit is not in its owning workload's template: Deployment nginx-thrift and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 both declare resources limits.memory=256Mi and requests.memory=128Mi for the nginx-thrift container, while the running pod carries limits.memory=16Mi and requests.memory=16Mi.
nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qtqx5 is the only pod in namespace social-network with any memory limit declared (limits/requests memory = 16Mi); the other 26 pods report no memory limit.

ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in namespace platform-ops holds server.py, an HTTPS admission-review server whose constant MEMORY = "16Mi" is written by a JSONPatch into container[0].resources.requests.memory and container[0].resources.limits.memory of every pod it admits (no label or name condition in the code).

All five MutatingWebhookConfigurations (cert-manager-webhook, gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, istio-sidecar-injector, kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config) use clientConfig.service name=platform-policy-controller, namespace=platform-ops, path=/mutate, port=443; webhook mutation.gatekeeper.sh in gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration matches apiGroups [""], resources [pods], operations [CREATE], scope Namespaced, namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network, with an empty objectSelector.

Deployment platform-policy-controller in namespace platform-ops runs the webhook (image python:3.12-alpine, command python /app/server.py, port 8443, ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server mounted at /app) and became available at 22:53:46Z (MinimumReplicasAvailable); its pod platform-policy-controller-7d44bbdc6b-7rv9w has been Running since 22:53:43Z with 0 restarts and limits.memory=128Mi (it is outside the webhook's social-network namespaceSelector).

The nginx-thrift pod that carries the injected 16Mi limit was created after the mutator went live: ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 created pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-7x7pn at 22:53:39Z (container started 22:53:41Z), that pod was stopped (Killing) at 22:53:54Z, and nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qtqx5 was created at 22:53:54Z with the nginx-thrift container started 22:53:55Z, i.e. after the platform-policy-controller was available at 22:53:46Z.

Deployment nginx-thrift is unavailable during the incident: status Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ('Deployment does not have minimum availability'), unavailableReplicas=1, and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="social-network",deployment="nginx-thrift"} is 0 at 22:53:30Z, 22:53:45Z and 22:54:00Z, while media-service and user-service read 1 at the same instants.

The client side of the social-network traffic observed failures: load-generator pod wrk2-job-jx6xv logged '  Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 42782, timeout 0' at 22:54:03Z and a burst of 'reconnect_socket' lines at 22:54:04Z, coinciding with the repeated OOMKill of the nginx-thrift front-end (that Loki result was itself incomplete at its 30-line limit).

The nginx-thrift container wrote openresty alerts 'worker process <N> exited on signal 11' at 22:53:54Z and 22:54:03Z (pods nginx-thrift-65f656c999-7x7pn and 65f656c999-qtqx5); the same signal-11 alerts also appear at 22:53:42Z and 22:53:52Z for the pre-mutation pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-cl8kw, so they are not unique to the 16Mi pod.

Jaeger's sample for nginx-web-server contains one trace only, at 22:53:48Z (span /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read with http.status_code=200 and children read_home_timeline_client / read_home_timeline_server / post_storage_read_posts_server, no error status), and the sample ends at 22:53:48Z, i.e. before the OOMKill loop started.

Deployment nginx-thrift carries a kubectl-patch Update at 2026-11-23T22:53:39Z (generation 2, revision 2) after the helm Apply at 22:53:15Z, and the events show the Deployment scaling up new ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 at 22:53:39Z and scaling old nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df down from 1 to 0 at 22:53:42Z; this rollout is what placed a fresh pod after the mutator was live, but the template in effect is 256Mi/128Mi.

The other application pods were not crashing: at 22:54:06Z all 26 other pods in social-network were phase Running with restartCount 0 and ready containers, including user-service, media-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service, jaeger and all redis/memcached/mongodb pods.

Checked media-frontend and found it not attributable to this cause: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="media-frontend"} was 0 at 22:53:30Z, 22:53:45Z and 22:54:00Z, but its pod media-frontend-864dc9bb45-8qmz9 was phase Running with its containers ready and restartCount 0 at 22:54:06Z, consistent with startup lag rather than a failure; its application log lines were not obtained.

Rejected: that nginx-thrift's own Deployment/Pod template sets the 16Mi limit. The Deployment and ReplicaSet templates both declare 256Mi limit / 128Mi request; only the admitted pod object carries 16Mi, so the value was introduced at admission, not by the workload spec.

Rejected: that a downstream dependency of nginx-thrift (home-timeline-service, post-storage-service, redis/memcached/mongodb backends) is the cause. The one sampled nginx-web-server trace at 22:53:48Z reached read_home_timeline_server (553us) and post_storage_read_posts_server (7us) with no error status, and those pods were Running with 0 restarts.

Mechanism: pods created in namespace social-network after the platform-policy-controller became available (22:53:46Z) are mutated to a 16Mi memory limit; openresty needs more than 16Mi, so the nginx-thrift container is OOM-killed seconds after start, loops in CrashLoopBackOff, the Deployment stays unavailable, and the wrk2 load generator's writes fail. The effective admitting webhook for these pods is mutation.gatekeeper.sh in MutatingWebhookConfiguration gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration (empty objectSelector); the kyverno, istio, linkerd and cert-manager entries require labels or resources that nginx-thrift pods do not carry.

Review and remove (or scope) the platform-policy-controller admission mutation and the MutatingWebhookConfigurations that route pod CREATE to it in namespace social-network; deleting pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-qtqx5 would only recreate it with the same 16Mi value while the webhook is active. A valid 256Mi/128Mi limit is already declared on the Deployment and ReplicaSet.

gaps: The platform-policy-controller container (pod platform-policy-controller-7d44bbdc6b-7rv9w) returned no log lines (its handler suppresses logging); that log read returned no_data, so the admission response that stamped 16Mi onto the nginx-thrift pod was not observed directly. The mutation is inferred from the pod vs ReplicaSet template mismatch and the hardcoded MEMORY = "16Mi" in ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total had no series in 22:30-22:54Z (get_series, instant and range queries all returned nothing: 4dd05feb-3e3d-4447-a213-fb2ba084ba22-t0:57cf4023-ea0c-4f11-9920-fa0d9de8f635, a6431299-bfc9-4f2d-b8af-808f420714bc-t1:30574e6a-1471-422e-a757-d71e0c899c8b, 5cffbcfc-c64a-4145-8d25-153477c91a49-t0:6a236929-352d-4eac-bc25-d82a650b20d2, 2ba77e37-a797-4e8e-86d1-0322629902c2-t1:46ece313-6221-46ec-a6ac-cdd523c72fcf); those empty results show only that the queries matched nothing, so error rates and status distributions are unmeasured, not zero.

Jaeger's sample ends at 22:53:48Z, before the OOMKill loop; no post-22:54:05Z trace coverage of failed requests exists in the returned sample, and the nginx-thrift pod log read (2261f2d3-8fdd-4980-970d-b1b4fd9868f2-t0:49d8b812-edcc-4cf5-b82e-14ff4f5a7f1a) returned no_data, so application-log confirmation from the crashing pod itself is missing.

media-frontend error lines were not observed: the Loki filter on that pod returned no_data (1a9fcccf-aa78-45f8-89f1-d33694da74c4-t1:2152bd15-1601-4cbc-83d6-29771be12039), so 'no error log' for media-frontend is unverified; only its Running/ready pod state was observed.

The wrk2-job log read was incomplete at its 30-line limit (89fbc543-b134-422c-89a6-a855317d74f9-t1:7cafdb85-03e2-49e0-9449-917d9d7ea9e3); errors it printed outside the returned lines are unknown, and the wrk2-job pod no longer exists (no jobs and no such pod are listed at query time).

Only events from 22:53:15Z onward survive in the cluster (208 social-network events, source_start_at 22:53:15Z), so when the MutatingWebhookConfigurations, the platform-ops Deployment and ConfigMap, and the kubectl-patch on Deployment nginx-thrift were created or changed before that instant is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
What the kubectl-patch at 22:53:39Z on Deployment nginx-thrift changed is not recorded beyond the resulting 256Mi/128Mi template (managedFieldsSummary gives only manager and time).
Secret platform-policy-controller-tls could not be read; whether the inspected webhook is the only mutator of pod resources cannot be verified beyond the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations listed.
next_steps: Inspect and, if unauthorized, remove the platform-policy-controller Deployment/ConfigMap in namespace platform-ops and the MutatingWebhookConfigurations whose clientConfig points to it, then verify a new nginx-thrift pod keeps its declared 256Mi limit.
Confirm with the cluster owner why the admission mutator was installed and whether it is intended to target only specific workloads or labels.

Add alerting on kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and OOMKilled terminations in the social-network namespace, and on kube_deployment_status_replicas_available below kube_deployment_spec_replicas.

import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return
